principles.mechanism: Write the tokens before any code: 4-6 named hex colours with roles, 1-2 typefaces with roles, one ASCII layout sketch. Check the sketch against the banned list first.
principles.principle: Commit to one bold aesthetic direction, named before any code, and spend your boldness in one place.

principles.mechanism: Take the idea from the thing itself: its materials, vocabulary, industry and users. Open the hero with the most characteristic thing — headline, image, animation or live demo.
principles.principle: Design from the subject, not from a template category.

principles.mechanism: One dominant colour + one sharp accent; neutrals tinted toward the brand hue; solid colour text only.
principles.principle: Colour discipline: dominant + accent, tinted neutrals, no washes.

principles.mechanism: Distinctive display + refined body pairing; modular scale with fluid clamp() sizing; lines under 80 characters; hierarchy by size and weight jumps, not just bold.
principles.principle: Type is the personality: a chosen pairing, a real scale, a felt hierarchy.

principles.mechanism: Real photos of this subject's world, real numbers, real copy in the user's words. Anything unsupported becomes a labelled proof gap or a question — never invented copy.
Every element earns its place. One accent + one theme per page. Ornaments rationed (at most 1 eyebrow per 3 sections).
principles.principle: Purposeful restraint: quiet sections let the loud one work.

principles.mechanism: Render in a real browser and screenshot at 320px / 768px / 1280px. Run deterministic lint rules, not vibes. Get a fresh-context reviewer.
principles.principle: Verify against reality, not against your own taste.
principles.source: Hallmark sloplint; Taste-Skill inspector; Impeccable detector

principles.mechanism: 1 primary + at most 1 secondary reference, each for a named dimension. Write down what was intentionally NOT copied. Blend at least 2 sources plus your own brand tokens.
principles.principle: One reference, for a named dimension — never one reference, copied.

principles.mechanism: Every sentence carries a claim, example, number, constraint or image. Active voice, real human subject, varied sentence length.
principles.principle: Generic writing is slop too: substance in every sentence.

principles.mechanism: Motion only to communicate state, hierarchy or continuity: trigger, move, settle, with real timing. Respect prefers-reduced-motion.
principles.principle: Motion with a job, or no motion.

source_note: Restated in our own words from the research report §1.2 and §5. Per-type principles below add craft rules on top of these ten universal principles.

ad.mechanism: One message in 10 words or fewer, one offer with exact verifiable price/deadline, one CTA. The hook is the most shocking verified fact, not a slogan.
ad.principle: An ad is one promise, proved, with one action.
ad.source: Research report §6 (ad intake); community ad practice

ad.mechanism: Design the hook first, then 2-3 variants that change the hook — not the same layout re-skinned. Test hooks, not colours.
ad.principle: Variants vary the idea, not the decoration.

ad.mechanism: Every claim must pass legal/compliance: disclaimers present, no before/after unless allowed, no invented results.

brand.mechanism: Define voice in 3 words, then derive palette, type and imagery from those words — not the other way round.
brand.principle: Brand is a voice with a visual system, not a logo with extras.

brand.mechanism: Ship the system, not the poster: tokens, type scale, spacing, radius, components, do/don't — in a DESIGN.md the team can actually follow.
brand.principle: A brand that cannot be written down cannot be repeated.

brand.mechanism: Test the identity at 16px favicon, 1-colour, embroidery and signage sizes before calling it done.
brand.principle: If it only works at poster size, it is not a brand.

logo.mechanism: One sentence for what the company does, 3 words for personality, then the mark type follows (wordmark / monogram / icon / combination). Never start with a shape.
logo.principle: The mark is the last decision, not the first.

logo.mechanism: Design in one colour first. If the idea dies in black on white, colour will not save it.
logo.principle: One-colour first: the idea must survive without decoration.
logo.source: Logo craft, restated from research report §5

logo.mechanism: List competitors' marks and name exactly how this one differs — shape, idea, or construction, not just colour.
logo.principle: Different on purpose, not different by accident.

social.mechanism: Design for the exact aspect ratio and safe area first (1:1, 4:5, 9:16). Text must be legible at feed size — no small or tiny text.
social.principle: Feed size is the real canvas; the artboard is not.
social.source: Research report §6 (social intake); user quality bar

social.mechanism: One message per post, one visual idea per post. A carousel earns each slide with a new idea, not a repeated look.
social.principle: One post, one idea, fully committed.

social.mechanism: The caption and the visual are designed together: the image stops the scroll, the caption earns the save/share/comment.
social.principle: Visual and caption are one artefact.

ui.mechanism: Map the flow first: onboarding, core action, success, empty, error, offline. Design the empty and error states with the same care as the happy path.
ui.principle: A UI is a flow with states, not a screen.

ui.mechanism: Every interactive element gets hover, focus, disabled, loading and error states, or a stated reason it does not. Focus must be visible.
ui.principle: States are the design, not the polish.

ui.mechanism: Use real content examples and edge cases (long names, empty lists, errors) while designing — never lorem in a UI.
ui.principle: Design with the ugliest real data, not the prettiest fake data.

ui.mechanism: Take patterns from shipped apps (flows, sections), not from concept shots. Label concepts as concepts.

web.mechanism: Name the one job of the page and the one action. Put proof (real numbers, named testimonials, logos with permission) before the pitch when trust is the objection.
web.principle: Proof before pitch when trust is the objection.

web.mechanism: Vary section compositions across the page. One radius system with intent. Hero fits its screen with CTAs visible without scrolling.
web.principle: An editorial grid, committed to for a reason — not centred everything.

web.mechanism: Every section carries full real content. A form destination must be real — never a fake 'thanks' form. SEO, meta and OG are part of the design, not an afterthought.
web.principle: A landing page is a working page, not a poster.
